ingredients.name: Fresh cilantro
ingredients.note: half for the dressing, half chopped on top

ingredients.name: Limes
ingredients.note: 3 juiced for the dressing, 1 in wedges

ingredients.name: Black beans
ingredients.note: cooked, or one 400 g can, rinsed

ingredients.name: Olive oil
ingredients.note: mild extra virgin, for the dressing

black-bean-sweet-potato-quinoa-salad.lunchbox: Made to be eaten cold and gets better after a night in the fridge (keeps 3 days). Pack the pepitas and the avocado separately and add them at lunch so they stay crisp and green.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C and line a sheet pan. Put the whole jalapeño on the pan.
Toss the sweet potato with 1½ tbsp neutral oil, the chili powder, ½ tsp smoked paprika, ¼ tsp cumin and ¾ tsp salt. Spread on the same pan.
Roast potatoes and jalapeño 20–24 min until fork-tender, turning the jalapeño once. Move the potatoes to a large bowl and chill; set the jalapeño aside.
Toss the pepitas with ½ tsp oil, a pinch of salt and ⅜ tsp paprika. Toast in the oven 6–7 min until golden. Let cool.
Bring the quinoa, 420 ml water and the remaining salt (keep about ⅜ tsp for the dressing) to a boil. Simmer uncovered 13–14 min, then cover off the heat for 5 min. Drain any extra water and chill.
Dressing: seed the roasted jalapeño. Blend it with the lime juice, garlic, ½ tsp cumin, ⅜ tsp salt and half the cilantro, then stream in the olive oil until smooth.

Add the cooled quinoa, black beans, spinach and green onions to the potatoes. Toss with about ¾ of the dressing, taste, add more if you like, and season with black pepper. Rest in the fridge about 1 hour if you have time.
Just before serving, stir in the pepitas, avocado and chopped cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.
black-bean-sweet-potato-quinoa-salad.title: Black bean, sweet potato & quinoa salad

chicken-cabbage-skillet.lunchbox: Keeps 3–4 days in the fridge; reheat 1–2 min in the microwave. Don't freeze it, the cabbage turns mushy. Scaled from 6 servings to 4, so it's a light portion on its own: add rice or noodles if you want a bigger lunch.
steps: Sauce: whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, garlic, honey, ginger, rice vinegar and sesame oil in a small bowl.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken, breaking it up, until no longer pink. Lift it out with a slotted spoon, drain the juices and wipe the pan.
Add the remaining oil. Cook the coleslaw mix and carrot 3–4 min, stirring, until tender-crisp. Lower the heat if they start to burn.
Return the chicken, add the sauce, season with salt and pepper and cook a few minutes until hot.
Stir in the green onions and cilantro. Serve with more cilantro, hot chili sauce and a squeeze of lime.
chicken-cabbage-skillet.title: Chicken & cabbage skillet

ingredients.name: Parsley
ingredients.note: leaves picked and chopped; 2 half-bunch sachets

ingredients.name: Smoked paprika
ingredients.note: 2 tsp for the pan, 2 tsp for the mash

ingredients.name: Milk
ingredients.note: a small splash for the mash; listed as 0.5 splash per portion

grilled-chicken-chorizo-parsnip-carrot-m.lunchbox: Store the mash, chicken and chorizo in separate airtight containers in the fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat everything until piping hot, adding a splash of milk to loosen the mash.
steps: Bring a pan of salted water to the boil.
Peel the carrots and parsnips and slice them into thin half-moons.
Simmer the carrots and parsnips for 24-26 minutes over medium-high heat until tender.
Finely chop the garlic and shallots, chop the parsley and crush the hazelnuts.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper on both sides.
Heat a splash of olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat.
Fry the shallots, garlic, parsley, hazelnuts, chorizo and 2 tsp smoked paprika for 3-4 minutes, then set aside on a plate.
Reheat the pan over medium-high heat and fry the chicken for 4-6 minutes per side until cooked through, adjusting for thickness.
Return the chorizo mixture to the pan at the end of cooking.
Check the vegetables with a knife tip, then drain them.
Blend the vegetables to a purée with a stick blender.
Stir in the butter, a splash of milk, salt, pepper and 2 tsp smoked paprika, then cover.
Spoon the mash onto plates and top with sliced chicken and the chorizo sauce.
grilled-chicken-chorizo-parsnip-carrot-m.title: Grilled Chicken, Chorizo & Parsnip-Carrot Mash

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.note: 2 for the lentils, 1 for the sauce

harissa-lentil-sweet-potatoes.lunchbox: Keep the sweet potatoes, the lentils and the tahini sauce in separate containers (up to 4 days). Reheat the potatoes and lentils, then add the tahini and parsley. If the sauce has thickened in the fridge, whisk in a splash of water and lemon.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C and line a sheet pan. Toss the sweet potato halves with 1 tbsp oil and a good pinch of salt, lay them cut side down and roast 50–60 min until soft and caramelised.
Meanwhile, heat 1 tbsp oil in a large pan over medium heat. Soften the shallots 3–4 min, then add 2 cloves of minced garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the tomato paste, harissa, smoked paprika and coriander and cook about 2 min, until the paste darkens.

Add the lentils and stir to coat. Pour in the broth with ½ tsp salt and some pepper. Bring to a boil, then simmer with the lid ajar 25–30 min until the lentils are tender and most of the liquid is gone.
Sauce: whisk the tahini, lemon juice and 1 grated garlic clove, then whisk in 3–4 tbsp water until pourable. Season with salt and pepper.
Uncover the lentils, stir in the kale and cook 2–3 min until wilted. Adjust the seasoning; add a splash of broth if it looks dry.
Put two sweet potato halves on each plate, fluff the flesh with a fork, spoon the lentils over, drizzle with tahini sauce and finish with parsley and pepper.
harissa-lentil-sweet-potatoes.title: Harissa lentil sweet potatoes

ingredients.name: Mango
ingredients.note: peeled, pitted, diced (1/3 mango per person)

ingredients.name: Piri-piri
ingredients.note: 1/2 tsp per person for the shrimp, plus a pinch for the mayo; adjust to taste

spicy-bowl-with-golden-shrimp-lemon-mang.lunchbox: Store the rice, shrimp, salad and spicy mayo in separate containers in the fridge and eat within 1-2 days. Pack the mayo separately, then reheat the rice and shrimp briefly or eat them at room temperature and add the fresh salad just before eating.
steps: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil for the rice.
Wash the lemons, zest them finely, then cut into wedges. Grate the garlic.
Cook the rice for 12-14 minutes until tender, then drain.
Stir in a pinch of lemon zest, the butter, salt and pepper. Cover and set aside.
Dice the cucumber. Peel and pit the mango, then dice it. Chop the cilantro.
Mix the mango, cucumber and cilantro in a bowl with a few drops of lemon juice, a pinch of zest, salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a pan over high heat and sear the shrimp for 3-4 minutes until cooked through. If the mango is not very ripe, sear it with the shrimp.
At the end of cooking, add the garlic and the piri-piri to the shrimp.
Mix the mayonnaise with a pinch of piri-piri and a few drops of lemon juice.
Serve the rice in shallow bowls and top with the shrimp and mango-cucumber salad.
Add a spoonful of spicy mayo on the side, sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve with the remaining lemon wedges.
spicy-bowl-with-golden-shrimp-lemon-mang.title: Spicy Bowl with Golden Shrimp, Lemon & Mango

ingredients.name: Plain flour
ingredients.note: 1 tbsp for the sauce, the rest for coating

ingredients.name: Vegetable broth
ingredients.note: or 1 stock cube + 500 ml boiling water

veg-katsu-curry.lunchbox: Pack the sauce and rice together and the katsu in a separate box so it stays crisp. Reheat the katsu in the oven or air fryer (about 8 min at 200 °C) rather than the microwave. Keeps 3 days in the fridge.
steps: Soften the chopped onion and carrot in the olive oil with a pinch of salt over medium-high heat, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the curry powder, coriander, cumin and turmeric and cook 2 minutes, then stir in 1 tbsp flour for 1 minute.
Add the broth a ladle at a time, stirring until it thickens. Simmer 5–10 minutes, blend smooth, then stir in coconut milk and soy sauce. Season.
Cook the rice.

Set out three dishes: seasoned flour, plant milk, and seasoned panko. Coat each veg round in flour, then milk, then panko. If it won't stick, whisk half the flour into the milk to make a thin batter instead.
Shallow-fry in sunflower oil over medium-high heat, 3–4 minutes per side, until golden and crisp. Drain on kitchen paper.
Serve rice with a ladle of curry sauce and 3 katsu pieces, topped with sliced green onion and chilli.
veg-katsu-curry.title: Veg katsu curry (sweet potato, squash & aubergine)
